text.p: Three condemned prison inmates will be executed on the same night in January, according to death warrants signed Tuesday by Arkansas Governor Mike Huckabee.
All three men, each convicted of murder, are to die by lethal injection on the night of Jan. 8.
"It's not a pleasant job, but it's the governor's responsibility to carry out the law," said Jim Harris, an assistant to Huckabee.
"All three inmates came back from the Supreme Court with their appeals denied at the same time, and that's the reason their executions were scheduled together," Harris said.
Two of the inmates, Paul Ruiz and Earl Denton, were convicted of killing two Arkansas law enforcement officers in 1976, but their final appeals were refused only weeks ago.
The third inmate, Kirt Wainwright, was condemned to death for killing a retail clerk in rural Arkansas in 1988.
"It's not a job we look forward to, but we're prepared to carry out the executions," said Dina Tyler, a spokesman for the Arkansas Department of Correction.
Attorneys for the three men said they were studying the possibility of further appeals.

Arkansas is the only state known to have performed a triple execution since the death penalty was reinstated by the U.S. Supreme Court more than 20 years ago. In 1994 Arkansas put to death three men convicted of the torture killing of a prominent businessman.
